intended_object: The induced subgraph G[X] of a multigraph G on a vertex set X: its vertex set is X and its edges are the edges of G whose ends both lie in X. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The vertex set is X. An edge e links x and y in the new graph exactly when it does in G and both x and y lie in X. This is the standard induced subgraph. Two things the structure needs are also handled. The symmetry proof goes through. The condition that edge ends lie in the vertex set is filled in by the `grind` autoparam, which works because x ∈ X is part of the link predicate. When X ⊆ V(G), the result is exactly the textbook G[X]. When X is not a subset of V(G), the extra vertices become isolated vertices. This is a harmless extension of the definition, and the docstring states it explicitly, so it is not an error. Mathlib has no other definition of induced subgraphs for this `Graph` (multigraph) structure. `SimpleGraph.induce` and `SimpleGraph.Subgraph.induce` belong to a different graph framework. The definition already uses arbitrary vertex and edge types, so it is not too narrow.
